sanskrit.deva:
स ईक्षतेमे नु लोकाश्च लोकपालाश्च ।
अन्नमेभ्यः सृजा इति ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa īkṣateme nu lokāś ca lokapālāś ca |
annam ebhyaḥ sṛjā iti || 1 ||

lines.iast: sa īkṣateme nu lokāś ca lokapālāś ca

padaccheda.iast: saḥ īkṣata ime nu lokāḥ ca lokapālāḥ ca annam ebhyaḥ sṛjai iti
padaccheda.deva: सः ईक्षत इमे नु लोकाः च लोकपालाः च अन्नम् एभ्यः सृजै इति

translations.text: He reflected: ‘Here now are the worlds and the guardians of the worlds; let me create food for them.’

notes: Śaṅkara: the Lord reflected: these worlds and guardians that I have created are joined with hunger and thirst, so they cannot subsist without food; let me therefore create food for the guardians. In the world, lords are seen to be free to favour and to restrain their own people; so the great Lord, being lord of all, is free to restrain and to favour all.
The e-text lacks the first sentences of this passage of the bhāṣya; they were read in the Advaita Śāradā text.

sanskrit.deva:
सोऽपोऽभ्यतपत् ।
ताभ्योऽभितप्ताभ्यो मूर्तिरजायत ।
या वै सा मूर्तिरजायतान्नं वै तत् ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
so 'po 'bhyatapat |
tābhyo 'bhitaptābhyo mūrtir ajāyata |
yā vai sā mūrtir ajāyatānnaṃ vai tat || 2 ||

lines.iast: yā vai sā mūrtir ajāyatānnaṃ vai tat
lines.deva: या वै सा मूर्तिरजायतान्नं वै तत्

padaccheda.iast: saḥ apaḥ abhyatapat tābhyaḥ abhitaptābhyaḥ mūrtiḥ ajāyata yā vai sā mūrtiḥ ajāyata annam vai tat
padaccheda.deva: सः अपः अभ्यतपत् ताभ्यः अभितप्ताभ्यः मूर्तिः अजायत या वै सा मूर्तिः अजायत अन्नम् वै तत्

grammar.en: past passive participle f. abl. pl.

translations.text: He brooded over the waters. From them, so brooded over, a solid form was born. That solid form which was born, that indeed is food.

notes: Śaṅkara: wishing to create food, the Lord brooded over those same waters named before. From them, as the material, was born a ‘solid form’: something dense, able to sustain, made up of the moving and the unmoving.

sanskrit.deva:
तदेनत्सृष्टं पराङत्यजिघांसत् ।
तद्वाचाजिघृक्षत् ।
तन्नाशक्नोद्वाचा ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनद्वाचाग्रहैष्यदभिव्याहृत्य हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad enat sṛṣṭaṃ parāṅ atyajighāṃsat |
tad vācājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknod vācā grahītum |
sa yad dhainad vācāgrahaiṣyad abhivyāhṛtya haivānnam atrapsyat || 3 ||

lines.iast: sa yad dhainad vācāgrahaiṣyad abhivyāhṛtya haivānnam atrapsyat

padaccheda.iast: tat enat sṛṣṭam parāṅ atyajighāṃsat tat vācā ajighṛkṣat tat na aśaknot vācā grahītum saḥ yat ha enat vācā agrahaiṣyat abhivyāhṛtya ha eva annam atrapsyat
padaccheda.deva: तत् एनत् सृष्टम् पराङ् अत्यजिघांसत् तत् वाचा अजिघृक्षत् तत् न अशक्नोत् वाचा ग्रहीतुम् सः यत् ह एनत् वाचा अग्रहैष्यत् अभिव्याहृत्य ह एव अन्नम् अत्रप्स्यत्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: This (food), once created, turned away and sought to flee. He sought to seize it with speech. He could not seize it with speech. If he had seized it with speech, one would have been satisfied by merely speaking of food.

notes: Śaṅkara: the food, created in front of the worlds and guardians for their sake, like a mouse within reach of a cat, thought ‘this eater of food is my death’, turned back and wished to get beyond its eaters: it began to run away. Seeing what the food intended, that lump which is the aggregate of the worlds and guardians, made up of body and organs, being the first-born and seeing no other eaters of food, wished to seize it with speech, by the act of speaking, and could not. Had that first-born embodied one seized it with speech, the whole world, being his effect, would be satisfied by merely uttering ‘food’; and this is not so; hence we understand that the first-born too could not seize it with speech.

sanskrit.deva:
तत्प्राणेनाजिघृक्षत् ।
तन्नाशक्नोत्प्राणेन ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनत्प्राणेनाग्रहैष्यदभिप्राण्य हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tat prāṇenājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknot prāṇena grahītum |
sa yad dhainat prāṇenāgrahaiṣyad abhiprāṇya haivānnam atrapsyat || 4 ||

lines.iast: sa yad dhainat prāṇenāgrahaiṣyad abhiprāṇya haivānnam atrapsyat

padaccheda.iast: tat prāṇena ajighṛkṣat tat na aśaknot prāṇena grahītum saḥ yat ha enat prāṇena agrahaiṣyat abhiprāṇya ha eva annam atrapsyat
padaccheda.deva: तत् प्राणेन अजिघृक्षत् तत् न अशक्नोत् प्राणेन ग्रहीतुम् सः यत् ह एनत् प्राणेन अग्रहैष्यत् अभिप्राण्य ह एव अन्नम् अत्रप्स्यत्

translations.text: He sought to seize it with prāṇa. He could not seize it with prāṇa. If he had seized it with prāṇa, one would have been satisfied by merely breathing upon food.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: what follows is the same.
Śaṅkara comments on mantras 4–10 together; his words are given under mantra 10.

sanskrit.deva:
तच्चक्षुषाजिघृक्षत् ।
तन्नाशक्नोच्चक्षुषा ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनच्चक्षुषाग्रहैष्यद्दृष्ट्वा हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tac cakṣuṣājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknoc cakṣuṣā grahītum |
sa yad dhainac cakṣuṣāgrahaiṣyad dṛṣṭvā haivānnam atrapsyat || 5 ||

lines.iast: sa yad dhainac cakṣuṣāgrahaiṣyad dṛṣṭvā haivānnam atrapsyat

padaccheda.iast: tat cakṣuṣā ajighṛkṣat tat na aśaknot cakṣuṣā grahītum saḥ yat ha enat cakṣuṣā agrahaiṣyat dṛṣṭvā ha eva annam atrapsyat
padaccheda.deva: तत् चक्षुषा अजिघृक्षत् तत् न अशक्नोत् चक्षुषा ग्रहीतुम् सः यत् ह एनत् चक्षुषा अग्रहैष्यत् दृष्ट्वा ह एव अन्नम् अत्रप्स्यत्

translations.text: He sought to seize it with sight. He could not seize it with sight. If he had seized it with sight, one would have been satisfied by merely seeing food.

notes: Śaṅkara comments on mantras 4–10 together; his words are given under mantra 10.

sanskrit.deva:
तच्छ्रोत्रेणाजिघृक्षत् ।
तन्नाशक्नोच्छ्रोत्रेण ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनच्छ्रोत्रेणाग्रहैष्यच्छ्रुत्वा हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tac chrotreṇājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknoc chrotreṇa grahītum |
sa yad dhainac chrotreṇāgrahaiṣyac chrutvā haivānnam atrapsyat || 6 ||

lines.iast: sa yad dhainac chrotreṇāgrahaiṣyac chrutvā haivānnam atrapsyat

padaccheda.iast: tat śrotreṇa ajighṛkṣat tat na aśaknot śrotreṇa grahītum saḥ yat ha enat śrotreṇa agrahaiṣyat śrutvā ha eva annam atrapsyat
padaccheda.deva: तत् श्रोत्रेण अजिघृक्षत् तत् न अशक्नोत् श्रोत्रेण ग्रहीतुम् सः यत् ह एनत् श्रोत्रेण अग्रहैष्यत् श्रुत्वा ह एव अन्नम् अत्रप्स्यत्

translations.text: He sought to seize it with hearing. He could not seize it with hearing. If he had seized it with hearing, one would have been satisfied by merely hearing of food.

notes: Śaṅkara comments on mantras 4–10 together; his words are given under mantra 10.

sanskrit.deva:
तत्त्वचाजिघृक्षत् ।
तन्नाशक्नोत्त्वचा ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनत्त्वचाग्रहैष्यत्स्पृष्ट्वा हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tat tvacājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknot tvacā grahītum |
sa yad dhainat tvacāgrahaiṣyat spṛṣṭvā haivānnam atrapsyat || 7 ||

lines.iast: sa yad dhainat tvacāgrahaiṣyat spṛṣṭvā haivānnam atrapsyat

padaccheda.iast: tat tvacā ajighṛkṣat tat na aśaknot tvacā grahītum saḥ yat ha enat tvacā agrahaiṣyat spṛṣṭvā ha eva annam atrapsyat
padaccheda.deva: तत् त्वचा अजिघृक्षत् तत् न अशक्नोत् त्वचा ग्रहीतुम् सः यत् ह एनत् त्वचा अग्रहैष्यत् स्पृष्ट्वा ह एव अन्नम् अत्रप्स्यत्

translations.text: He sought to seize it with the skin. He could not seize it with the skin. If he had seized it with the skin, one would have been satisfied by merely touching food.

notes: Śaṅkara comments on mantras 4–10 together; his words are given under mantra 10.

sanskrit.deva:
तन्मनसाजिघृक्षत् ।
तन्नाशक्नोन्मनसा ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनन्मनसाग्रहैष्यद्ध्यात्वा हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tan manasājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknon manasā grahītum |
sa yad dhainan manasāgrahaiṣyad dhyātvā haivānnam atrapsyat || 8 ||

lines.iast: sa yad dhainan manasāgrahaiṣyad dhyātvā haivānnam atrapsyat

padaccheda.iast: tat manasā ajighṛkṣat tat na aśaknot manasā grahītum saḥ yat ha enat manasā agrahaiṣyat dhyātvā ha eva annam atrapsyat
padaccheda.deva: तत् मनसा अजिघृक्षत् तत् न अशक्नोत् मनसा ग्रहीतुम् सः यत् ह एनत् मनसा अग्रहैष्यत् ध्यात्वा ह एव अन्नम् अत्रप्स्यत्

translations.text: He sought to seize it with the mind. He could not seize it with the mind. If he had seized it with the mind, one would have been satisfied by merely thinking of food.

notes: Śaṅkara comments on mantras 4–10 together; his words are given under mantra 10.

sanskrit.deva:
तच्छिश्नेनाजिघृक्षत् ।
तन्नाशक्नोच्छिश्नेन ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनच्छिश्नेनाग्रहैष्यद्विसृज्य हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tac chiśnenājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknoc chiśnena grahītum |
sa yad dhainac chiśnenāgrahaiṣyad visṛjya haivānnam atrapsyat || 9 ||

lines.iast: sa yad dhainac chiśnenāgrahaiṣyad visṛjya haivānnam atrapsyat

padaccheda.iast: tat śiśnena ajighṛkṣat tat na aśaknot śiśnena grahītum saḥ yat ha enat śiśnena agrahaiṣyat visṛjya ha eva annam atrapsyat
padaccheda.deva: तत् शिश्नेन अजिघृक्षत् तत् न अशक्नोत् शिश्नेन ग्रहीतुम् सः यत् ह एनत् शिश्नेन अग्रहैष्यत् विसृज्य ह एव अन्नम् अत्रप्स्यत्

translations.text: He sought to seize it with the generative organ. He could not seize it with the generative organ. If he had seized it with the generative organ, one would have been satisfied by merely emitting food.

notes: Śaṅkara comments on mantras 4–10 together; his words are given under mantra 10.

sanskrit.deva:
तदपानेनाजिघृक्षत् ।
तदावयत् ।
सैषोऽन्नस्य ग्रहो यद्वायुः ।
अन्नायुर्वा एष यद्वायुः ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad apānenājighṛkṣat |
tad āvayat |
saiṣo 'nnasya graho yad vāyuḥ |
annāyur vā eṣa yad vāyuḥ || 10 ||

padaccheda.iast: tat apānena ajighṛkṣat tat āvayat saḥ eṣaḥ annasya grahaḥ yat vāyuḥ anna-āyuḥ vai eṣaḥ yat vāyuḥ
padaccheda.deva: तत् अपानेन अजिघृक्षत् तत् आवयत् सः एषः अन्नस्य ग्रहः यत् वायुः अन्न-आयुः वै एषः यत् वायुः

words.meaning: that which has its life in food

translations.text: He sought to seize it with apāna. He took it in. This air (apāna) is the seizer of food; this air is that which has its life in food.

notes: Śaṅkara: unable to seize the food with prāṇa, with sight, with hearing, with the skin, with the mind, with the generative organ, by the working of each organ in turn, he at last sought to seize it with the air apāna, through the opening of the mouth. So he seized the food: he ate it. Hence this air apāna is the ‘seizer’ of food, that which grasps food. The air that is well known as bound to food, as living by food, is this air.

sanskrit.deva:
स ईक्षत कथं न्विदं मदृते स्यादिति ।
स ईक्षत कतरेण प्रपद्या इति ।
स ईक्षत यदि वाचाभिव्याहृतं यदि प्राणेनाभिप्राणितं यदि चक्षुषा दृष्टं यदि श्रोत्रेण श्रुतं यदि त्वचा स्पृष्टं यदि मनसा ध्यातं यद्यपानेनाभ्यपानितं यदि शिश्नेन विसृष्टमथ कोऽहमिति ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa īkṣata kathaṃ nv idaṃ mad ṛte syād iti |
sa īkṣata katareṇa prapadyā iti |
sa īkṣata yadi vācābhivyāhṛtaṃ yadi prāṇenābhiprāṇitaṃ yadi cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭaṃ yadi śrotreṇa śrutaṃ yadi tvacā spṛṣṭaṃ yadi manasā dhyātaṃ yady apānenābhyapānitaṃ yadi śiśnena visṛṣṭam atha ko 'ham iti || 11 ||

lines.iast: sa īkṣata kathaṃ nv idaṃ mad ṛte syād iti
lines.deva: स ईक्षत कथं न्विदं मदृते स्यादिति

lines.iast: sa īkṣata yadi vācābhivyāhṛtaṃ yadi prāṇenābhiprāṇitaṃ yadi cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭaṃ yadi śrotreṇa śrutaṃ yadi tvacā spṛṣṭaṃ yadi manasā dhyātaṃ yady apānenābhyapānitaṃ yadi śiśnena visṛṣṭam atha ko 'ham iti
lines.deva: स ईक्षत यदि वाचाभिव्याहृतं यदि प्राणेनाभिप्राणितं यदि चक्षुषा दृष्टं यदि श्रोत्रेण श्रुतं यदि त्वचा स्पृष्टं यदि मनसा ध्यातं यद्यपानेनाभ्यपानितं यदि शिश्नेन विसृष्टमथ कोऽहमिति

padaccheda.iast: saḥ īkṣata katham nu idam mat ṛte syāt iti saḥ īkṣata katareṇa prapadyai iti saḥ īkṣata yadi vācā abhivyāhṛtam yadi prāṇena abhiprāṇitam yadi cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭam yadi śrotreṇa śrutam yadi tvacā spṛṣṭam yadi manasā dhyātam yadi apānena abhyapānitam yadi śiśnena visṛṣṭam atha kaḥ aham iti
padaccheda.deva: सः ईक्षत कथम् नु इदम् मत् ऋते स्यात् इति सः ईक्षत कतरेण प्रपद्यै इति सः ईक्षत यदि वाचा अभिव्याहृतम् यदि प्राणेन अभिप्राणितम् यदि चक्षुषा दृष्टम् यदि श्रोत्रेण श्रुतम् यदि त्वचा स्पृष्टम् यदि मनसा ध्यातम् यदि अपानेन अभ्यपानितम् यदि शिश्नेन विसृष्टम् अथ कः अहम् इति

translations.text: He reflected: ‘How indeed could this be without me?’ He reflected: ‘By which (of the two ways) shall I enter?’ He reflected: ‘If speaking is done by speech, breathing by prāṇa, seeing by sight, hearing by hearing, touching by the skin, thinking by the mind, breathing down by apāna, emitting by the generative organ, then who am I?’

notes: Śaṅkara: having thus made the subsistence of the aggregate of worlds and guardians depend on food, as a lord settles that of a city, its citizens and their keepers, he reflected: how could this aggregate of body and organs, which exists for another, be without me, the lord of the city? Speaking by speech and the rest, if they were all, would be quite purposeless, like the tribute and praises that citizens and bards offer for a lord when there is no lord. Therefore I, the supreme, the lord, the overseer, the witness of the fruit of what is done and left undone, must be the enjoyer, as a king is of a city. If this aggregate could be for another without me, the conscious one for whom it is, ‘then who am I’: of what nature, and lord of what? If I did not enter the aggregate of body and organs and perceive the fruit of what speech and the rest utter and do, as a king enters a city and looks into what his officers have done and left undone, no one would come to know me as ‘he exists and is of such a nature’. But in the other case I can be known: he who knows the speaking of speech and the rest as ‘this’ exists and is of the nature of awareness, and for his sake is the speaking and the rest of the combined organs; as pillars, walls and the like, combined into a palace, exist for another who is not combined with their parts.

Śaṅkara: having so reflected, ‘by which shall I enter?’ The tip of the foot and the head are the two ways into this aggregate; by which of these two ways shall I enter this city, the aggregate of body and organs?

sanskrit.deva:
स एतमेव सीमानं विदार्यैतया द्वारा प्रापद्यत ।
सैषा विदृतिर्नाम द्वाः ।
तदेतन्नान्दनम् ।
तस्य त्रय आवसथास्त्रयः स्वप्ना अयमावसथोऽयमावसथोऽयमावसथ इति ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:

lines.iast: sa etam eva sīmānaṃ vidāryaitayā dvārā prāpadyata
lines.deva: स एतमेव सीमानं विदार्यैतया द्वारा प्रापद्यत

lines.iast: tasya traya āvasathās trayaḥ svapnā ayam āvasatho 'yam āvasatho 'yam āvasatha iti
lines.deva: तस्य त्रय आवसथास्त्रयः स्वप्ना अयमावसथोऽयमावसथोऽयमावसथ इति

padaccheda.iast: saḥ etam eva sīmānam vidārya etayā dvārā prāpadyata sā eṣā vidṛtiḥ nāma dvāḥ tat etat nāndanam tasya trayaḥ āvasathāḥ trayaḥ svapnāḥ ayam āvasathaḥ ayam āvasathaḥ ayam āvasathaḥ iti
padaccheda.deva: सः एतम् एव सीमानम् विदार्य एतया द्वारा प्रापद्यत सा एषा विदृतिः नाम द्वाः तत् एतत् नान्दनम् तस्य त्रयः आवसथाः त्रयः स्वप्नाः अयम् आवसथः अयम् आवसथः अयम् आवसथः इति

translations.text: Having cleft this very parting (of the hair on the head), he entered by this door. This door is named Vidṛti, ‘the cleft’. This is the place of delight. He has three dwellings, three dreams: this is a dwelling, this is a dwelling, this is a dwelling.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: having so reflected, ‘I will not enter below, by the tips of the feet, which is the way of entry of my servant prāṇa, who is set over all my affairs; what remains is that I cleave its head and enter’; like one in the world who acts after reflection.

Śaṅkara: the Lord, the creator, cleft this parting on the head, where the dividing of the hair ends, made an opening, and by this door entered this world, the aggregate of body and organs. This door is well known: when oil or the like is held on the head, its taste and the like are felt within. It is named Vidṛti because it was cleft. The other doors, the ears and the rest, are common ways, like those used by servants, and so are not rich, not sources of joy; this door is the supreme Lord's alone, so it is nāndana, that is nandana, ‘the delight’ (the long vowel is Vedic): going by this door one delights in the supreme Brahman.

Śaṅkara: of him who, having so created, entered as the jīva, like a king a city, there are three dwellings: in the time of waking the seat of the senses, the right eye; in the time of dream the mind within; in the time of deep sleep the space of the heart. Or they are the three to be described (in adhyāya 2): the father's body, the mother's womb, and one's own body. The three dreams are those called waking, dream and deep sleep. Is not waking, being wakefulness, no dream? It is a dream indeed: because there is no waking to one's own real Self, and because unreal things are seen in it as in a dream. ‘This is a dwelling’: the right eye is the first, the mind within the second, the space of the heart the third; it only repeats what was said. Abiding in these dwellings in turn, taking them for himself, fast asleep for a long time through the ignorance that is natural to him, he does not wake even on feeling the blows of the hammer of pain that come from the falling upon him of many hundreds of thousands of evils.

sanskrit.deva:
स जातो भूतान्यभिव्यैख्यत्किमिहान्यं वावदिषदिति ।
स एतमेव पुरुषं ब्रह्म ततममपश्यदिदमदर्शमिती ३ ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa jāto bhūtāny abhivyaikhyat kim ihānyaṃ vāvadiṣad iti |
sa etam eva puruṣaṃ brahma tatamam apaśyad idam adarśam itī 3 || 13 ||

lines.iast: sa jāto bhūtāny abhivyaikhyat kim ihānyaṃ vāvadiṣad iti
sa etam eva puruṣaṃ brahma tatamam apaśyad idam adarśam itī 3

padaccheda.iast: saḥ jātaḥ bhūtāni abhivyaikhyat kim iha anyam vāvadiṣat iti saḥ etam eva puruṣam brahma tatamam apaśyat idam adarśam iti
padaccheda.deva: सः जातः भूतानि अभिव्यैख्यत् किम् इह अन्यम् वावदिषत् इति सः एतम् एव पुरुषम् ब्रह्म ततमम् अपश्यत् इदम् अदर्शम् इति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Born (having entered the body as the jīva), he distinguished the beings: ‘What here would one speak of as other?’ He saw this very Puruṣa as Brahman, the most pervading: ‘This I have seen!’

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘born’: having entered the body as the jīva. He ‘distinguished’ the beings: he made them distinct (by name and form). When at some time a most compassionate teacher beat close to his ear the great drum of the sayings of the Vedānta, whose sound wakes one to the knowledge of the Self, he woke to, he saw, this very Puruṣa, the one spoken of as the maker of the creation and the rest, the Self that lies in the city (of the body), as Brahman, the great, tatama: that is tata-tama with one ‘ta’ dropped, the most pervading, full like space. How? ‘I have seen this Brahman, the real nature of my Self. Oh!’ The prolonged vowel (itī3) expresses reflection.
Śaṅkara does not gloss the words kim ihānyaṃ vāvadiṣat; the meaning and translation give their plain sense. vāvadiṣat is a Vedic form of the intensive of vad.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मादिदन्द्रो नाम ।
इदन्द्रो ह वै नाम ।
तमिदन्द्रं सन्तमिन्द्र इत्याचक्षते परोक्षेण ।
परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmād idandro nāma |
idandro ha vai nāma |
tam idandraṃ santam indra ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa |
parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ || 14 ||

lines.iast: tam idandraṃ santam indra ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa
parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ
lines.deva: परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः

padaccheda.iast: tasmāt idandraḥ nāma idandraḥ ha vai nāma tam idandram santam indraḥ iti ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣa-priyāḥ iva hi devāḥ parokṣa-priyāḥ iva hi devāḥ
padaccheda.deva: तस्मात् इदन्द्रः नाम इदन्द्रः ह वै नाम तम् इदन्द्रम् सन्तम् इन्द्रः इति आचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्ष-प्रियाः इव हि देवाः परोक्ष-प्रियाः इव हि देवाः

translations.text: Therefore his name is Idandra; Idandra indeed is his name. Him, who is Idandra, they call Indra, indirectly; for the gods are fond, as it were, of the indirect; for the gods are fond, as it were, of the indirect.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: because he saw Brahman, the innermost of all, directly and immediately, as ‘this’ (idam).

Śaṅkara: because he sees ‘this’ (idam), the supreme Self is named Idandra; as the Lord he is well known in the world by that name. The knowers of Brahman, for the purpose of ordinary dealings, call him Indra, by an indirect name, fearing to take the direct name of him who is most to be revered. For even the gods are fond of being named indirectly; how much more the great Lord, the god of all the gods. The repetition marks the end of the adhyāya.
